brief:
Israel's latest election delivered a fragmented parliament, the Quincy Institute reported, setting the stage for protracted coalition negotiations. No single party secured a commanding majority, leaving multiple political blocs vying to assemble a governing coalition. The outcome reflects deepening divisions within Israeli society across ideological and security-related fault lines.

Coalition-building typically involves weeks of bargaining among parties with competing demands and priorities. The fractured result complicates efforts to form a stable government and may empower smaller parties to extract concessions on their key policy concerns.
title: Israeli election produces fractured result as coalition talks begin
